runners_data.name: Little Lady Karen
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's filly has placed twice from two starts on Good ground and steps up slightly in trip to 7f which should suit her staying profile; Sam James rides and she switches from hold-up to a likely closer-to-the-pace role in this small field.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile has a busy recent form profile (5 runs) with four placing efforts on Good or similar; Jason Hart takes over and the headgear (p) suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up, though her hold-up style needs a genuine gallop to be seen at her best.

runners_data.name: Dakota Brave
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's colt is a genuine hold-up horse whose best chance depends on a strong pace that this race is unlikely to generate; last ran 14 days ago and has course-applicable form at 7f, but the Good to Firm conditions and compressed field make it hard for him to deliver his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's runner has shown modest form in three starts all on Good ground at shorter trips, and stepping up to 7f is an unknown quantity; his natural closing style is similarly compromised by the lack of strong pace, and the style-fit discount is warranted given the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Hamdani Mokhater
runners_data.note: James Horton's gelding carries the lowest weight at 121lbs and, as a natural prominent racer, finds himself mapped to the front by default with no genuine pace in the race; has placed twice at 7f on Good going which are directly relevant conditions, and Ray Dawson's experience of the situation could prove decisive if he controls the tempo.

races.paceDynamic: Hamdani Mokhater, a natural prominent racer redistributed to the lead in this map, is the most likely pace-setter by default in a field where no confirmed front-runner exists — he sets a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground over Catterick's flat seven furlongs. With only five runners and the entire field composed of hold-up and prominent types, the pace is unlikely to be strong, creating a falsely-run race that compresses the field through the middle stages. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Dakota Brave and Bigalo are both true closers mapped to midfield, with Hamdani Mokhater most likely to actually secure the early lead ahead of them. A moderate gallop on fast ground at this trip strongly favours runners who can travel prominently and quicken from the front or just off it, rather than late closers who will find little pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hamdani Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hamdani Mokhater gets the run of the race at a comfortable clip and kicks clear entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With no genuine front-runner to force the pace, Hamdani controls tempo throughout and has first run on the field off the final bend; on Good to Firm ground the leader gets a significant advantage in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Karen or Koodini travel prominently enough to challenge Hamdani Mokhater for the lead early and the race develops into a two-or-three-way duel.
scenarios.body: A modest pace duel between the top two in the market sets a more honest gallop, opening the door for a stronger staying effort in the closing stages; both Little Lady Karen and Koodini have placed form and the trip suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Kick
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving something for late finishers.
scenarios.body: Dakota Brave and Bigalo, both true hold-up types, would need a strong pace to reel in the leaders — unlikely on these going conditions with this small, pace-light field; even if the scenario unfolds, both are racing out of their ideal position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race is tactically chaotic with positional jostling throughout, leaving no runner able to dictate.
scenarios.body: An unpredictable early order disrupts every horse's rhythm; in this five-runner field on fast ground, however, this outcome is rare and would most likely hand an advantage to the lowest-weight runner with fresh legs.

watchPoints.text: Hamdani Mokhater — if he gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm, he may be very difficult to reel in with only five runners and no genuine pace-pressing rival.

Koodini — the addition of headgear (p) for Hugo Palmer suggests a significant stable intention; watch for her to be ridden more prominently than her hold-up tag suggests, which could alter the early pace order.

Dakota Brave and Bigalo — both are true hold-up types placed in midfield on the map; if the pace is as moderate as expected, watch whether Rowan Scott or Kevin Stott elect to push their mounts forward early to avoid getting stranded with no pace to chase.

Little Lady Karen — stepping up from 6f to 7f for the first time; watch whether Sam James drops her in behind or rides her more positively given the lack of confirmed pace in this small field, as her role could define the race shape significantly.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer on good ground at 7f but sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 5 similar surfaces is damaging; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps the weight, visored for focus, but 9 days since last run is fine — needs a pace that doesn't materialise here.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: David Allan partners a horse with two places at 7f on good or good-to-firm in recent starts; tongue-tied for the first time, which can spark improvement, and a record of travelling prominently means he should sit close to Good Karma naturally — the best-placed hold-up-leaning runner in the field given this tempo.

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby runner who won over this C&D in good going on his penultimate start and hit the frame again last time; a genuine closer by inclination but nudged into midfield on the map because of overcrowding at the rear — Dale Swift will need to find a position closer to the pace than usual to exploit the form credentials.

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-maker who won over 7f at Southwell last time out; John David Riches has just one runner in the past fortnight so limited trainer momentum, and 37 days off is worth noting — but with nothing to challenge him early, Sean Kirrane can dictate this completely from the front.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's seven-year-old showed a win over 6f on good last time and has placed form at 7f on good ground; a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the weight of closers in this field — Aiden Brookes will struggle to get her into her rhythm without a searching pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Young Fahey three-year-old with solid placed form at 7f on good going; Warren Fentiman takes a 3lb claim off the top, which is useful at this level, but this horse's entire profile is built around having a genuine pace to chase — racing off a slow front-set by Good Karma is far from ideal.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's three-year-old carries a visor and has a modest recent record; figures in form of 0s and 8s tell their own story, and the redistribution into midfield compounds the problem of needing a true pace to deliver from the back — Shane Gray has little pace-flow to exploit here.

runners_data.name: Patontheback
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran for Gemma Tutty who has not troubled the judge in any of his last five 7f starts on similar ground; Rowan Scott rides, and while the horse has historical placed form, the combination of age, current OR, and being bumped into midfield from a natural hold-up position makes this a tough assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Good Karma is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 7f handicap at Catterick and, with no genuine rival willing or able to match strides from the gate, Sean Kirrane should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground without being pressured at any stage. That moderate, uncontested tempo is unlikely to produce a truly searching test, and the lack of a pace duel means the field will be compressed into a bunch approaching the final two furlongs, rewarding those who can travel handy and deliver a sharp, late kick rather than those who need a strong pace to reel rivals in. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Vega Storm, Kings Merchant, Wise Crack, Ideal Guest and Patontheback are all genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing in unfamiliar midfield positions, meaning none can be confident of producing their natural finish; of those, Kings Merchant, with a recent course-and-distance win and a wider draw, is best placed to negotiate the compromise. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape heavily favours a prominent racer who can slot just behind Good Karma and pounce when the sprint is triggered, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the absence of genuine early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Good Karma Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma secures the lead without a murmur and sets a steady-moderate gallop that keeps the field bunched.
scenarios.body: Good Karma dictates every yard on the front end, the pace is comfortable enough to sustain it to the line, and no hold-up horse gets the strong pace required to close from far back; Vince Le Prince, travelling prominently, is best placed of the chasers to strike in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma sets a fair pace but a prominent-tracking rival produces a decisive turn of foot rounding the final bend.
scenarios.body: Kings Merchant or Vince Le Prince tracks the leader at close range, waits for the sprint and gets first run on the field as the closers are too far back to respond; good-to-firm ground and a flat 7f at Catterick suits horses who travel with ease and have a late gear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma goes off faster than expected and the gallop becomes genuinely strong, creating a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo would compress the field and allow the handful of genuine hold-up types shuffled into midfield to close through beaten rivals in the final furlong; Kings Merchant, with course form at this trip in good going, and Ideal Guest, whose recent 6f win on good shows she retains ability, are the most likely beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — All-The-Way
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma is never headed and the entire field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: A very slow, unchallenged gallop can sometimes see a front-runner simply extend clear in the final furlong as rivals are denied the pace to organise their challenge; this scenario requires the hold-up horses to fire poorly and the field to be too slow to react.

watchPoints.text: Good Karma's absence of any early pressure is the defining tactical fact — watch whether Sean Kirrane elects to dawdle and steal this from the front, as no rival has the style or desire to chase him down early.

Kings Merchant's true running style is that of a closer yet he is likely to find himself in midfield without the strong pace he prefers — watch for Dale Swift improvising by pushing forward to track Good Karma, which could dramatically change this horse's chance.

Vince Le Prince's tongue-tie is applied for the first time today; a significant piece of headgear change on a horse with recent placed form at 7f on good ground is worth monitoring in the market and in the early stages of the race.

With five genuine hold-up types competing for a small patch of racing room in the rear half of the field, watch for crowding and interference as the field compresses — any horse forced widest at the two-furlong pole will carry a major disadvantage on the flat Catterick straight.

The going report confirms good-to-firm conditions for this race; any horse with a concern flag or a soft-ground preference in its recent history should be treated with caution, and the firmer surface will further benefit those who travel prominently rather than those waiting for a late gap.

races.name: racingtv/freetrial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Steel Fixer
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 3yo has been placed over 1m6f on good ground and the step back to 1m4f could suit; a natural hold-up horse with zero wins and no places on similar going (0W0P from 3 runs), so relies on pace being stronger than this race shape is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner with a T14 strike rate of 3/22, so the stable is in decent form; showed one placing on good ground but has six runs without a win and the lack of natural pace in this race is a significant structural negative for a horse who wants to come from off it.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 3yo holds the best recent form in the field — a win and a place on similar ground — and carries a hood; a true hold-up horse by nature but the map moves it forward given the field composition, meaning its best chance arises if it can settle just off the pace rather than being pushed too far back in a slowly-run race (STYLE_FIT: 0.92).

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends out nine winners per fortnight (T14:9/72) and this horse carries the pace-setting role by default rather than natural inclination — it is a prominent type rather than a genuine front-runner — making the pace sustainable rather than forcing; blinkers applied, six runs from nine on good ground suggest it handles conditions but the unnatural role tempers its chance (STYLE_FIT: 0.80).

runners_data.name: Clova Royale
runners_data.note: Peter Niven horse with a 0/2 trainer 14-day record and a consistent history of finishing eighth or worse on good ground (four from four without a placing on this going); tagged as fading in the finish and genuinely held up by nature yet mapped to midfield, so the combination of poor recent form, fade flag and out-of-role positioning makes this one hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's yard sends two from sixteen over the past fortnight; all recent runs have been on standard (Tapeta/Fibresand) and there is no turf or good-ground evidence to draw from — that unknown quantity, combined with the fade warning and being a true hold-up horse repositioned in midfield, means this is a difficult profile to trust on this surface today.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Tokyo
runners_data.note: 168 days off the track is a notable concern for this 3yo who has three starts, all on standard surfaces, with the best finish an eighth — the lack of turf or good-ground evidence, combined with the longest absence in the field and a fade flag, leaves this horse with the weakest profile overall; a true hold-up type shown in midfield only because the rear is overcrowded.

races.paceDynamic: Fairydale is the lone pace-setter here, redistributed to the front from a hold-up profile, meaning this race will be run at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over 1m4f on good-to-firm ground at Catterick — there will be no pressure on the leader and the fractions are likely to be controlled throughout. The field behind Fairydale is stacked with genuine hold-up horses: Riddikulus, Clova Royale, Project Kinsman and Spirit Of Tokyo are all true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for all of them at the rear, but their natural instinct will be to settle and come late. With a lone leader dictating a modest pace, those hold-up horses face the classic problem of needing a strong gallop that will not materialise, making it hard to generate sufficient momentum for a finish-line surge on a flat track. The tactical verdict is clear: a genuine front-runner or prominent racer who can stalk the steady pace and quicken from close to the leader holds the structural advantage, and horses who require a strong pace to deliver their finishing kick are compromised by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fairydale Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fairydale bowls along in front at a steady clip and no rival has the natural pace or position to apply pressure.
scenarios.body: Fairydale leads throughout at a comfortable tempo, the field strings out behind without a real surge developing, and the winner is drawn from horses racing prominently who never get far off the pace; with all the hold-up horses trapped wider or deeper than ideal, the leader or a close stalker simply outstays them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a midfield tracker can sit just off Fairydale's shoulder through the final bend and produce a decisive kick in the straight.
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits a horse who slots in second or third and has enough tactical speed to kick when asked; Riddikulus, despite being a true hold-up type pushed forward, has the best recent form in the field and could capitalise if it settles close enough to the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts enough in the final three furlongs to string the field out and create a genuine finishing test.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the tempo to increase materially — which is structurally unlikely given only one pace-setter — but if it does, horses with strong finishing kicks such as Sound Gloria or Steel Fixer could find room and close; both carry [STYLE_FIT] concerns through redistribution, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Fairydale's unnatural role at the front leads to a very slow crawl that produces a sprint finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A dawdle sets up a bunched finish where any of the midfield horses can win on raw speed rather than stamina, but Clova Royale and Project Kinsman both carry fade warnings and have weak recent form, making them vulnerable; this scenario is the least predictable and least likely given the going description.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Fairydale actually takes up the lead or drifts back to its natural hold-up position — if no horse leads, the race could crawl at a dangerously slow early pace that renders all pace-shape analysis redundant.

Riddikulus is a hold-up horse mapped forward by the tool; if it fails to settle in a handy position and gets outpaced to the rear, its strong recent course-and-distance form becomes much harder to convert.

Clova Royale and Project Kinsman both carry fade-in-finish flags — if either moves prominently early and then stops, it could create trouble for horses trying to come through in the straight on this flat track.

The going is described as Good To Firm throughout the card at Catterick today despite the headline "Good" going — horses with a concern flag on firmer ground should be monitored before the off, as the going report data indicates faster conditions than the race card suggests.

races.name: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has placed twice over 10f on Good going; Faye Bramley's yard is 2/5 in the last 14 days and Clifford Lee partners well, but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 suggests it may not entirely relish having to go from the front rather than tracking — monitor early keenness.

runners_data.name: Something
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty's mount arrives in excellent form (1W4P over 12f on Good), having won a 12f handicap most recently and placed four times in five; the natural prominent profile suits tracking Explode here and the OR of 77 looks workable against this field.

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's string is in exceptional form (7/65 in 14 days) and Jason Hart is a quality booking, but this horse is inherently a prominent racer and, with the prominent slots already occupied, it will likely be shuffled wider and back than ideal — its GOO sim-going record (12/15 runs) is strong but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's four-year-old has two recent wins over 12f on Good and Firm ground and Tudhope is a high-class retention, giving it genuine upside on raw ability; however, its natural inclination is to race up with the pace, and the hold-up position it occupies on the map reflects redistribution rather than preference — expect it to travel more prominently than the map suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Explode is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of four, and with only Something pushing from a prominent berth, the early pace is unlikely to be truly searching over 1m4f at Catterick. Explode should stride into a clear lead unchallenged, setting a measured, controlled tempo that rewards those who can track and sustain rather than those needing a dramatic late injection of pace. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Something is the likeliest to secure a genuine tracking position, while L'Eagle Aid and Hibernate are both natural prominent racers who have been mapped back due to that crowding and are unlikely to get their preferred spots close to the pace. This shape strongly favours a front-runner or a close tracker who can pounce before the race opens up, rather than a hold-up horse attempting to close from a position they do not naturally occupy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Explode Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Explode breaks cleanly and dictates a comfortable solo lead at his own pace with no serious pressure applied.
scenarios.body: Explode settles into a rhythm unchallenged and, with a sustainable gallop over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground, has enough in reserve to hold on when the field tries to close. A front-runner allowed to control fractions on quick ground is the dominant profile here, and Something is the only genuine threat from a genuine tracking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Something tracks Explode closely throughout and produces a well-timed surge to collar the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Something's recent form — three runs in the top three over 12f on Good ground — makes it the natural beneficiary if the pace is just quick enough to expose Explode late. The tracking position suits its profile, and the OR drop from its peak means it arrives with a live each-way profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Explode sets a frantic early pace that burns itself out, allowing the field to converge in the straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the gallop to be genuinely unsustainable, which seems unlikely given Explode's natural style is comfortable front-running rather than tearaway. L'Eagle Aid — a true prominent type pushed back on the map — would theoretically benefit most, but its redistribution away from its natural position makes delivering a sustained late run from the rear unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hibernate Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the field dawdles early and Hibernate, finding its best form over ground and trip, produces a strong finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: Hibernate has shown genuine ability (two wins in recent form, 2W7P on similar going) and Tudhope is a top jockey, but the horse's natural style is prominent and it has been mapped back purely due to field compression. A winning hold-up effort would require it to race entirely against its instincts, making this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Something exerts any pressure on Explode in the first half-mile — if it sits tight and tracks, the two will likely fight out the finish; if it drops away early, Explode wins with a margin.

L'Eagle Aid's early positioning is a key flashpoint — if Jason Hart attempts to muscle up to a prominent spot and forces a contested early pace, Explode's controlled lead scenario is undermined and the race becomes far more open.

Hibernate travelling forward early would confirm the redistribution caveat — if Tudhope sends it up to track the leaders rather than settling at the rear, the race shape compresses and the straight becomes a multi-horse scramble.

The going report lists all six races at Catterick as Good to Firm despite the declared Going showing Good — monitor any late adjustment, as a firmer surface would further favour Explode maintaining its lead without being reeled in.

races.name: Racing Again 4th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Highfield Sunshine
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Quinn yard who has placed in similar good-ground 6f/7f races but finds winners elusive; Jason Hart's booking is positive but 46 days off the track and a visor change warrant watching to see how quickly she settles from the rear.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's mare is the sole confirmed pace-setter and has won twice and placed heavily on good going at 5-6f; racing just 13 days ago keeps her fit and fresh, though her STYLE_FIT flag is minor — she is simply running from a slightly deeper-drawn pace role than her freshest form suggests.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Whisper
runners_data.note: Ron Barr's 4-year-old holds no wins and only two places from 15 similar-ground efforts, which represents a concerning profile-to-price ratio; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim helps on weight but the overall evidence on good ground and at 6f is weak, and the heavy headgear entry does not sharpen the picture.

runners_data.name: Howzak
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey runner who landed a 6f handicap on standard ground earlier this season, giving him a live form reference, but his true style is a deep hold-up horse whose one good-ground run in 15 produced no placing; naturally he wants to come late, which the lack of real pace in this race makes structurally difficult.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old owns the strongest raw form in the field, having won and placed on good ground at 5-6f multiple times including a recent win eight days ago; a pure hold-up type by instinct but David Allan will be keen to compromise toward midfield so the horse can travel closer and not get caught cold if Miss Rainbow rolls along at a trot.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's gelding has placed twice at 6f on good ground and races just four days after his last run, suggesting freshness is not an issue; Joanna Mason's booking adds tactical nous and his prominent style means he is well-placed structurally to sit just off the pace and challenge, though he has not won in 5 outings this year.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who, at OR 45, is the lowest-rated runner in the field and whose best form came over a mile-plus on standard ground; the redistribution to midfield is a mapping necessity rather than his preference, and his recent 3rd over 6f on good ground is encouraging, but Andrew Mullen will need the pace to fold dramatically for him to reach the principals.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Rainbow is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 6f handicap and, with no other genuine pace-setter to pressurise her, she is likely to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Catterick. Howzak, Barmyblade, and Wait For It are all natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because the field is back-heavy; none of them are likely to be anywhere near the lead, meaning Miss Rainbow faces minimal early pressure. The prominent types — Mister Sky Blue and Highfield Sunshine — may track but neither is a genuine challenger for the front, so Miss Rainbow should settle into an uncontested rhythm through the first half of the race before the field strings out on Catterick's straight run-in. This race shape strongly favours hold-up finishers with a sharp turn of foot if the pace is genuinely slow, but if Miss Rainbow controls a fair clip, prominent trackers who can sit close and conserve energy through the race will be best placed; given the compressed field and the likely lack of a searching gallop, runners able to race prominently without over-exerting will have a structural edge over the true hold-up horses who, though shown in midfield, will struggle to find enough late momentum from the rear on a track that does not always reward deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Rainbow Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow bowls along unchallenged at a fair but manageable clip and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough late momentum.
scenarios.body: Miss Rainbow, ridden by William Pyle, dictates every fraction from stall to straight and simply sustains her effort to the line, with no genuine pace-presser to force her wide or into an unsustainable tempo; Mister Sky Blue, racing close throughout, is ideally positioned to challenge if she ties up but Barmyblade's good-ground form at 6f gives it the best profile to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Clear Field
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow and Mister Sky Blue press each other slightly harder than expected, raising the tempo and suiting those who track just behind.
scenarios.body: A modestly elevated pace benefits runners sitting third or fourth who can slot in behind the speed and produce a straightforward sustained effort; Highfield Sunshine, held up but not too far back, and Barmyblade, with a strong good-ground 6f record including a recent win, are the profile types who collect if the lead pair tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop turns out to be deceptively fast and the field concertinas inside the final furlong, giving the true back-markers a route through.
scenarios.body: Barmyblade has the best raw good-going speed figures of the hold-up group and, despite being mapped to midfield, remains the most dangerous of the rear-ward runners if gaps open late; however, Howzak and Wait For It carry REDISTRIBUTED tags meaning their natural position is further back than the map shows, so this scenario is structurally compromised by the lack of genuine closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow goes too slow and the race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out, benefiting horses who save energy in the pack.
scenarios.body: A dawdle-then-sprint on Catterick's straight finish effectively turns this into a five-horse race, and horses with the best finishing speed rather than stamina will dominate; Woodhay Whisper, while without a win on the board here, has placed at 5f and could find this more speed-oriented shape marginally more conducive, but the overall quality of the hold-up group on their best going figures is modest.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Miss Rainbow is able to stride straight to the front unchallenged from the off — if Mister Sky Blue pushes her early, the tempo could rise sharply and undermine her chance of sustaining it to the line.

Barmyblade's jockey David Allan will need to bridge the gap between this horse's natural hold-up instinct and the need to be closer given a lack of true pace — if Allan sits too far back, Barmyblade may not get to the leaders in time on Catterick's relatively short straight run-in.

Howzak and Wait For It are genuine closers mapped into midfield artificially — if both drift back to their natural positions, the rear of the field becomes very congested and any interference in the final two furlongs could end their chance entirely.

Good-to-firm ground has been called for this race — Woodhay Whisper has just 2 places from 15 similar-ground runs, and any punter using her should factor in that the conditions historically do not suit her profile.

Trainer Liam Bailey saddles two runners (Howzak and Wait For It) at the same meeting with the same 37-day absence — worth monitoring which of the two Bailey appears to have primed as the first string, given both carry no headgear and have similar profiles.
